title: Strategy's bitcoin buying hinges on one number: STRC at $100
summary: What is happening Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, bought no bitcoin in the week of October 19 to 25. Instead it spent $204.9 million buying back its own STRC preferred shares, according to its October 26 filing with the SEC. Those buybacks have helped lift STRC to about $99.36, its highest level in roughly five months and just shy of its $100 par value. Social media accounts have run with the next step: Michael Saylor is "set to resume heavy Bitcoin buying" once STRC gets back to $100. That claim rests on a real, stated plan. Whether it plays out as "heavy" is a different question, and readers may get some answers soon. Strategy reports third-quarter results after the US close on Thursday, October 29, with a webinar at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time. What STRC is and why $100 matters STRC, nicknamed Stretch, is a perpetual preferred share with a variable dividend that Strategy pays monthly. The dividend is adjusted to keep the price anchored near its $100 par value, and Strategy raised the rate to 12% during the summer slump. The $100 level matters because Strategy has said it will not sell new STRC below par. Above it, STRC becomes a fundraising tool again: Strategy can sell shares into the market and use the cash to buy bitcoin. It still has about $17.5 billion of STRC available to sell under its at-the-market (ATM) programme, and that figure has not moved in its weekly filings since at least June.
